bug_semantics: Karakeep's public NextAuth credentials login (POST /api/auth/callback/credentials) reaches CredentialsProvider.authorize() in apps/web/server/auth.ts, which calls validatePassword() and then either issues a session cookie or returns a normal CredentialsSignin failure. Until the 2026-07-04 patch there was no in-product rate limit, failed-attempt lockout, CAPTCHA, or backoff on that path, so an unauthenticated client could send unlimited password guesses against a known email (CWE-307 / CWE-799). bcrypt cost 10 is the only inherent slowdown and does not stop online stuffing of weak or reused passwords. Signup later gained tRPC rate-limit middleware and optional Turnstile; login never did, because it is not a tRPC procedure.
flaw_origin: The unthrottled password-login mechanism was first written in 942aac691225f4895c159a0260890ad2c576e0c9 (2024-02-22, 'feature: Add support for credentials registration and sign in'). That commit added next-auth CredentialsProvider plus authorize()/validatePassword() in packages/web/server/auth.ts (later moved to apps/web/server/auth.ts) with a try/catch that maps any auth failure to null and no attempt-frequency control. Immediate parent 08e7cbcfcb5e0b992d10ada324712c224b7a4d07 only configured Authentik SSO and API-key bcrypt; git grep of the parent tree finds no CredentialsProvider, authorize(), or validatePassword(). Later edits (fail2ban logging, logger removal, db argument, event logs, directory moves) are refactors/carriers, not a new first-write of the unthrottled login.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-75773 / GHSA-2ccr-52p8-6754 is a published CWE-307 finding on the NextAuth credentials login authorize() path. First-party issue #2919 plus a working oracle (session cookie vs CredentialsSignin) show unlimited pre-auth password guesses. The maintainer treated it as a real bug and landed f7d042971d0d2bcc7119654830cf1eb93eabbf24; CVE.org is PUBLISHED, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. BIC search used -L/-S/blame on authorize() and did not start from AI-marked commits. The smallest public first-write of the unthrottled login is 942aac691225f4895c159a0260890ad2c576e0c9; its parent tree lacks any credentials login, the commit is not a merge/squash with reconstructable members, and later auth.ts edits only log, pass db, or move the file. Rate-limit infrastructure appearing later on tRPC (signup etc.) is omitted-control relative to login, not a new first-write of the vulnerable lines. AI is judged only on that BIC commit object: human maintainer MohamedBassem as author and committer, empty trailers, no bot. Therefore NOT_AI.
